root_cause.defect: DEFECT E — ENCODED RANGE REPRESENTATION PASSED TO FROZEN PARSER
root_cause.mechanism: The pinned client sends Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate. For a RANGED request SEC serves a byte range of the COMPRESSED representation. The transport called gzip.decompress() on that fragment, it raised, and one line swallowed it (`except (OSError, zlib.error, EOFError): body = raw`). Compressed bytes reached the frozen parser as document bytes.
root_cause.compounding: Two independent errors: range offsets referring to the compressed representation while the frozen spine assumes document-byte semantics, and a decode failure falling back to raw instead of failing closed. Either alone would have been visible; together they produced a plausible, self-consistent and entirely false picture across three canaries.
root_cause.proof: Accession 0000912057-00-024277: 28,350 retained bytes are a gzip stream (1f8b) decompressing to 106,350 bytes containing <SEC-HEADER> at 423, 'STANDARD INDUSTRIAL CLASSIFICATION: PHARMACEUTICAL PREPARATIONS [2834]' at 748, and </SEC-HEADER> at 1,169. The SIC was always there.

refuted_hypotheses.sic_lies_beyond_byte_4095: REFUTED — the SIC is at decompressed offset 748, inside the ORIGINAL 4 KiB window
refuted_hypotheses.historical_archive_lacks_sic_or_sec_head: REFUTED — both present and correctly terminated
refuted_hypotheses.why_recorded: so a later reader who encounters the header-completion machinery does not infer that the theories which motivated it remained factual

the_fix.scope: the legacy ranged fallback ONLY; all other request semantics unchanged
the_fix.rationale: structural rather than clever — obtain the representation the frozen spine already assumes, instead of teaching the transport to incrementally decompress arbitrary encoded byte ranges
the_fix.client_untouched: verified: a per-request Accept-Encoding overrides the pinned client's default without modifying client.py (6c1d7006)
the_fix.fail_closed: `except ...: body = raw` is gone from every parser-facing path. An undecodable body yields NO body. ACQUISITION_ENCODING_UNSUPPORTED is stamped BEFORE raising, so the spine's fail-soft handler cannot convert a machinery failure into an apparent absence of SIC.
three_overlapping_guards: decode state — an outright decoding failure

encoded-body integrity invariant — content_encoding non-identity AND wire_bytes > 0 AND sha256_body == sha256_wire means decoding never happened. This signal was present in EVERY failed canary and nothing was checking it.
gzip magic — a concrete escaped encoding, catching the case where nothing is declared and the hash invariant is therefore blind
the_fix.zero_length_guard: gzip.decompress(b'') returns b'' rather than raising, so an empty encoded body decodes successfully and correctly passes. The guard prevents a SPURIOUS failure; it does not manufacture one.

retention_invariant.rule: persist EXACTLY the parser-facing bytes used for the SIC decision; do not trim at </SEC-HEADER>
retention_invariant.boundaries: recorded as OFFSETS INTO THE PERSISTED BYTES (sec_header_open_offset, sec_header_close_offset), not decoded-text character positions, so they carry no encoding-dependent ambiguity
retention_invariant.custody_chain: SEC response -> decode -> parser-facing bytes -> persisted exact bytes -> frozen parser (one transformation shorter than trimming, and materially easier to audit)
retention_invariant.not_outcome_dependent: bytes are kept for every filing, not only failures — retaining evidence only where the result was interesting is how a corpus acquires a selection bias nobody can later measure

fixture_corrections_in_the_validation_re.why_recorded: Both were FALSE-GREEN risks, not cosmetic test cleanup. They are why the final regression suite actually exercises the production failure mode.
fixture_corrections_in_the_validation_re.mocktransport_decoded_at_stream: httpx.Response(content=...) DECODES at .stream iteration, so httpx raised before the transport ever saw the bytes and the guard was never exercised. The real HTTPTransport yields undecoded wire bytes — which is precisely why the live canary retained gzip. Fixtures now build responses with stream=ByteStream(...).
fixture_corrections_in_the_validation_re.fixture_document_was_too_compressible: the document gzipped to 255 bytes, so a 4 KiB range returned a COMPLETE gzip stream that decoded fine and the fragmented-gzip case never occurred. The fixture now carries deterministic, poorly-compressible filler.
